facts.text: Newaygo’s name may come from Ojibwe Chief Nuwagon or an Algonquian word meaning "much water," reflecting the area’s river heritage.
The town’s first saw mill was built by brothers at Penoyer Creek, sparking a long‑lasting lumber industry in Newaygo County.
The Big Red Mill on the east bank of the Muskegon River survived as a lumber mill, cement plant, and grain storage into the present day.
The Muskegon River runs through Newaygo, offering popular canoe trips, tubing, and fishing for locals and visitors alike.
During the late 1800s, the river’s log‑floating system made Newaygo a key hub for transporting lumber to Muskegon’s mills.
The City Museum showcases artifacts that chronicle Newaygo’s rich local history, from its founding to modern times.
